findings_addressed: FIX-4 [P2] 1/2 — THE INJECTED PUBLISHED-SOURCE WAS NEVER EXERCISED THROUGH run_survey (test_registry.py, AC-SBOM-17). The criterion called classify_status(ecosystem, locked, latest) DIRECTLY, so Slice 32 could ship a correct comparator while run_survey(..., published=...) NEVER CALLED published.latest() and left every staleness row 'unknown' — and AC-SBOM-15/16 would still pass, because both of those inject a source (OfflineSource, ExplodingSource) that LEGITIMATELY yields 'unknown' for everything, so neither can distinguish 'the source was asked and returned nothing' from 'the source was never asked'. That left THE USED-VS-PUBLISHED DIFF — the output this whole tool exists to produce — completely untested end to end. CLOSED by a second leg on AC-SBOM-17 that drives a POSITIVE StaticSource THROUGH run_survey and asserts on the resulting STALENESS ROWS: one package mapped to its own locked version must come back status='current', a second mapped to 9999.0.0 must come back 'outdated', a third mapped to 0.0.1 must come back 'ahead', each with latest_version equal to the INJECTED value (which is what proves the row carries the source's answer rather than a coincidence), and EVERY package absent from the mapping must stay status='unknown' / latest_version=None — that last row is what stops a blanket fill from passing the first three. The three probe packages are picked FROM A PRECEDING OFFLINE RUN rather than hardcoded, so the leg cannot rot when a lockfile moves; they are constrained to a UNIQUE (ecosystem, name) — npm package-lock v3 can emit the same name at two versions (§5.5) — and to a plain major.minor.patch with major >= 1, so that both sentinels order unambiguously under BOTH comparators (semver rejects 1.2.3.post1, PEP 440 rejects 1.2.3-rc.1, so a sentinel must parse under either). Leg 1 SURVIVES because the comparator matrix it grades — semver prereleases, PEP 440 .postN, unparseable input, either side missing — cannot be provoked from whatever this repository happens to have locked. Design §5.4 carries the four-row probe table and the reasoning; §4's AC-SBOM-17 row now states both legs.

FIX-4 [P3] 2/2 — THE --describe TIER VOCABULARY WAS NOT ASSERTED (test_cli.py, AC-SBOM-19). §5.9 and the test's OWN failure message require --describe to publish the tier vocabulary, but the assertion set (ci_gating is False, recurring is True, name == 'sbom-survey') would pass unchanged if the command OMITTED `tiers` entirely or returned the wrong values — so downstream tooling could not discover the ruled vocabulary without importing the package, while AC-SBOM-19 was green. CLOSED by asserting `tiers` is PRESENT (with the key set printed on failure) and that tuple(described['tiers']) == TIER_VOCABULARY == ('shipped', 'dev-tooling', 'eval-only'), IN THAT ORDER. The ORDER is now stated in the spec of record too (§5.9: 'shipped first, because it is the tier that outranks the others in Slice 33's triage'), so the test and the design cannot drift into disagreeing about whether a sorted list would do.

FIX-4 SWEEP — THE POINT OF THIS ROUND. Both round-4 findings are the SAME structural defect, and it is the THIRD round to produce it: round 2 finding 2 was fixture exclusion proven at TierMap.classify() but not at the run_survey boundary; round 4 finding 1 is status comparison proven at classify_status() but not at the run_survey boundary; round 4 finding 2 is a CLI field required by contract but never asserted for content. The class: A CRITERION IS GRADED AGAINST A HELPER OR SUB-FUNCTION WHILE THE INTEGRATION BOUNDARY THAT ACTUALLY HAS TO CALL IT GOES UNGRADED. Rather than let the remaining instances surface one per round, ALL 23 CRITERIA were swept with the question 'could Slice 32 satisfy this test while run_survey() — or the CLI — never actually does the thing the requirement demands?'. FOUR MORE INSTANCES FOUND AND CLOSED, all within their existing criteria's stated subjects: (a) AC-SBOM-01 — the injected ls_files runner proved discover_manifests(), NOT run_survey(); a filesystem walk inside run_survey pulling target/**/Cargo.toml or node_modules/**/package.json passed. Now every fathomdb:declared-in origin in the emitted document must be a path `git ls-files` reports, with a vacuity guard that at least one origin exists. (b) AC-SBOM-02 — same shape; 'python/ is out of BOM SCOPE' is a statement about the emitted BOM, so no origin may be under python/. (c) AC-SBOM-11 — it asserted only that fathomdb:tier held A VALUE FROM THE VOCABULARY, which is precisely the shape of the [P3] just filed: an implementation stamping 'dev-tooling' on all ~400 components passed while EVERY TIER IN THE DOCUMENT WAS WRONG, and Slice 33 prioritises on exactly that field. The tag must now EQUAL TierMap.classify(<its declaring manifest>).tier, scoped to components with EXACTLY ONE fathomdb:declared-in origin — a package declared by two manifests of different tiers has no single ruled answer in §5.2/§5.3 and demanding one would have invented a contract — with a guard that at least one component was graded that way. (d) AC-SBOM-20 — bomFormat and specVersion are two strings any file can carry, so the sbom.cdx.json the CLI actually WROTE was effectively ungraded while AC-SBOM-10 graded only the in-process to_cyclonedx() object; the written artifact now goes through the same INDEPENDENT upstream CycloneDX 1.6 validator. (e) AC-SBOM-22 — the Slice-33 field set and sort order were graded on Survey.staleness(), which SLICE 33 NEVER CALLS: it opens staleness.json, so report.write_reports() could project a poorer row shape with the criterion green. The written artifact is now asserted to be exactly {generated, source, summary, rows} with source == 'offline' for an --offline run, every row carrying the field set, in the ruled sort order. The full 23-row sweep — INCLUDING the rows that legitimately needed nothing, each with its reason — is tabulated in design §13.2 rather than left implicit.

FIX-4 SWEEP, THE DELIBERATE NO-OPS (stated, not skipped; full table in §13.2). AC-SBOM-03: completeness of the CANDIDATE SET is a discovery contract, and a per-path boundary assertion is NOT DERIVABLE — lockfile paths never appear as declared_in (§5.5) and a manifest that declares nothing legitimately contributes no origin; its boundary consequences are covered by AC-SBOM-01's new leg (nothing untracked), AC-SBOM-08 (every discovered path is tiered) and AC-SBOM-10 (all three purl types present). AC-SBOM-04: ecosystem/kind on a ManifestRef is a pure unit contract whose boundary reflection is the document's purl-type set, already asserted EXACTLY {cargo, npm, pypi}. AC-SBOM-05/06/12/13/14/15/16/21: already at the boundary. AC-SBOM-07: its boundary halves are AC-SBOM-21 (CLI exit 2 naming the path) and AC-SBOM-06's stripped-map run_survey leg. AC-SBOM-08: enforced at the boundary BY CONSTRUCTION — if tiers.toml did not cover every discovered manifest, every run_survey call in the suite would raise. AC-SBOM-09: a constant, whose two boundary reflections are AC-SBOM-11 (component tags) and, from this round, AC-SBOM-19 (--describe). AC-SBOM-13: grading the fathomdb:constraint VALUE would require the test to re-implement the manifest parsers, so the falsifiable halves are kept (presence on every direct component; a version that is not a range). AC-SBOM-18: CONSIDERED AND DECLINED — asserting the CLI DEFAULTS --out to DEFAULT_REPORT_DIR would require a CLI run that writes into the TRACKED repository tree, which every CLI test here deliberately avoids (all use tmp_path). AC-SBOM-23: TierMap.classify() is where longest-prefix matching lives and AC-SBOM-06 already proves run_survey consults the injected map's RULE SET; the boundary tie is closed from the other end by AC-SBOM-11's new agreement assertion, so a matcher re-implemented inside run_survey must agree with the graded one.

FIX-4 IN PASSING — the known-invalid NEGATIVE CONTROL moved INSIDE conftest.independent_cyclonedx_validator(), so it runs once before the validator is returned and EVERY caller receives an oracle already shown to bite. AC-SBOM-10 KEEPS its own explicit control assertion — that is where the reasoning is documented and it costs nothing — and design §5.7 records both facts.
